purpose: Verify that retiring RenderPlan camera.dof.aperture and deriving the renderer kernel gain from the canonical f_stop leaves raw pixels unchanged.
fixture: Optical Studio 1920x1080, 30 fps, DoF enabled, same generated assets and scene. Current Motion plan regenerated from the dirty working tree; baseline raw frames are the pre-migration software-render outputs archived in camera-closure-final.
wire_check: camera.dof and camera_samples[*].camera.dof contain enabled, focus_distance, max_blur, highlight_gain; no aperture, f_stop or iris aliases nested under dof. f_stop and iris_blades remain camera-level.

render.command: chronon3d_cli render --plan CURRENT_PLAN --assets-root WORKSPACE --backend software --video-sink raw --pipe-pixfmt rgba --encoder-backend pipe --start-frame FRAME --end-frame FRAME

new_required_camera_producers: plan_optical_studio: 4/4 image layers and camera use 150 resolved transform/camera samples; no integer TRS animation remains.
plan_word_rack_focus: 7/7 image/text/shape layers and camera use 151 resolved samples; no integer TRS animation remains.
plan_map_flyover --camera-backed: requests the V3 resolved sample contract; geospatial test confirms the map plate and camera share the sample calendar.
motion_geospatial camera-backed test producer: V3 resolved layer samples verified.
resolved_sample_migration.null_controller: Motion Null/controller layers are no longer emitted as transparent Color layers in RenderPlan; their world transforms are flattened into content/camera samples.
resolved_sample_migration.still_legacy: plan_documentary_showcase includes Particle and Adjustment layers, which C3D transform_samples validation currently rejects. It remains on integer TRS tracks until those consumer types have an explicit resolved-sample contract.

scope_limit: Exact DoF wire/render equivalence is demonstrated for three pinned software raw sentinels. The resolved-sample producer migration is partial: documentary Particle/Adjustment and any unenumerated consumers remain legacy. This does not claim full-video equivalence, Vulkan equivalence, or AE visual parity.
